newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares up, but could fall back on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares up, but could fall back on Wall St.

text.p: Danish share prices closed up on Monday, driven by dollar-sensitive stocks, but dealers feared that the local market would be hit on Tuesday by Monday's higher-than-expected U.S. personal spending data.
"The American numbers could well take shares down a little," a dealer said. January U.S. consumption rose 0.7 percent, against an expected 0.6 percent.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.73 point to 153.70, in relatively modest overall bourse turnover of 975 million crowns.
The KFX March future rose 0.95 point to 153.25 with 532 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Dollar-sensitive Novo Nordisk gained 13.5 crowns, to 631.5 and Tele Danmark climbed nine crowns to 344.00, despite fears it will lose revenue under pending legislation giving rivals access to its network at what are expected to be sharply reduced rates.

Cleaning group ISS, like Novo and Tele Danmark also traded in New York, fell two crowns despite the strong dollar, on Friday's announcement that its vice-president and chief financial officer was quitting over strategic differences with fellow-directors.
